saints.name: St. Porphyry of Gaza
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A monk of the Egyptian desert made bishop of pagan Gaza, who by prayer and patience won that stubborn city for Christ…
biography: Born about 347 at Thessalonica, Porphyry left his wealth at twenty-five for the monks of the Egyptian desert of Skete, then lived five years as a hermit by the Jordan. Ordained priest at Jerusalem in 393 and made keeper of the relic of the True Cross, he was consecrated bishop of Gaza in 395 at the age of forty-five.

Gaza was then a stronghold of paganism, its Christians scarcely three hundred, and a drought was at once blamed on the newcomer's ill luck. His deacon Mark, who wrote his Life, records his patience amid insult; an imperial order closing the temples in 398 left the great shrine of Zeus Marnas open, for the official sent was bribed.

In the winter of 401-402 he went himself to Constantinople and won from the empress Eudoxia a decree of destruction, executed in May 402: the Marneion was burned with pitch and sulphur, and on its site rose the church called Eudoxiana, dedicated in 407. By his death on 26 February 420 the faith had taken firm root in Gaza.
saints.knownFor: The conversion of pagan Gaza to the Christian faith.

sources.text: Mark the Deacon, Life of St. Porphyry of Gaza (public-domain translation)
